Amsterdam. Founded as a fishing village in the thirteenth century, it rose to become the world's wealthiest city by the sixteen hundreds through the Dutch East India Company's monopoly on spices and Asian trade. Built on concentric canals engineered for both defense and commerce, Amsterdam attracted merchants, artists, and religious refugees, earning a reputation for tolerance unusual in early modern Europe. Home to Rembrandt and Vermeer, it became a model of civic organization and housed the world's first modern stock exchange.
